title: One focus per screen
statement: Give each screen one primary thing to attend to.
detail: The walkthrough of a built Grade 3 lesson applies an attention standard distilled from reviews: each screen has a single thing to attend to, because attention is the scarcest resource and split screens split learning, and help appears at the step that uses it, never stacked upfront, because support on arrival is clutter and support at the point of use is scaffolding (`downloads/SUPERSEDED — see v2.1_ WITW Lesson 1 learning walkthrough v2 (table format).md`, lines 27 and 28; `downloads/SUPERSEDED — see v2 (table format)_ WITW Lesson 1 learning walkthrough.md`, line 13). No outcome was measured.

the original course experience opened by dumping authored diagram prose, repeated labels, a "look closely" guide, and mismatched narration instead of one obvious Grade 5 action
One ask at a time. Screen clutter is a pedagogical defect, not a cosmetic one.
**Name the ONE primary.** Every screen has exactly one thing the child must attend to. If you cannot name it, the page is two pages — split it.
